Simulate a Model Matrix and a Response Vector

Source: R/auxiliary.R
simulXy.Rd

Generates covariates (multivariate normal with AR(1) correlation) and a response from a Gaussian, binomial, Poisson or Gamma regression model, for simulation studies and examples.

Usage

simulXy(
  n,
  p,
  interc = 0,
  beta,
  family = gaussian(),
  prop = 0.1,
  lim.b = c(-3, 3),
  sigma = 1,
  size = 1,
  rho = 0,
  scale.data = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  X = NULL,
  dispersion = 0.1
)

Arguments

n

number of observations.

p

number of covariates.

interc

the intercept of the linear predictor (default 0).

beta

vector of p regression coefficients; if missing, a proportion prop of coefficients is drawn uniformly in lim.b and the others are zero.

family

a family object, function or name: gaussian, binomial, poisson or Gamma (with any of their links).

prop

proportion of non-null coefficients when beta is missing (default 0.1).

lim.b

range of the non-null coefficients when beta is missing.

sigma

standard deviation of the Gaussian response.

size

number of trials of the binomial response; with size > 1 the response is a two-column matrix of failures and successes.

rho

correlation parameter: \(cor(X_j, X_k) = \rho^{|j-k|}\).

scale.data

logical: should the columns of the model matrix be standardised?

seed

optional seed; the state of the random number generator of the session is restored on exit.

X

optional model matrix replacing the generated one.

dispersion

dispersion parameter of the Gamma response (default 0.1).

Value

A list with components

data

a data frame with the response y (columns y.failure, y.success when size > 1) and the covariates X1, ..., Xp;

beta0

the intercept;

beta

the regression coefficients.

See also

islasso(), islasso.path()

Author

Gianluca Sottile gianluca.sottile@unipa.it

Examples

n <- 100; p <- 100
beta <- c(runif(10, -3, 3), rep(0, p - 10))
sim <- simulXy(n = n, p = p, beta = beta, seed = 1234)
str(sim$data[, 1:5])
#> 'data.frame':	100 obs. of  5 variables:
#>  $ y : num  -3.411 7.985 -7.269 0.904 1.386 ...
#>  $ X1: num  -1.046 0.432 1.236 -2.179 0.583 ...
#>  $ X2: num  0.362 -0.5 0.024 -0.527 -0.84 ...
#>  $ X3: num  0.3443 0.5647 0.0322 0.5688 0.1636 ...
#>  $ X4: num  -0.5445 -0.8999 -0.1631 0.9692 0.0302 ...
